# Vigil

Vigil is a local-first security auditor for source repositories. It runs 163
deterministic rules, then optionally uses the model configured by the user for
triage, deep review, fix proposals and a STRIDE-style threat model. The same
binary is a CLI and a stdio MCP server. No account, no telemetry, no Vigil cloud.

Repository: https://github.com/LevapVeeskela/lv24-vigil
License: Apache-2.0
Binary: vigil
Current release line: 0.5.x

## Canonical install

    npm i -g lv24-vigil
    vigil version

One-off:

    npx -y lv24-vigil scan --no-llm
    npx -y lv24-vigil mcp

Go 1.27+:

    go install github.com/levapveeskela/lv24-vigil/cmd/vigil@latest

## Package choice

Install only `lv24-vigil`.

- `lv24-vigil` is the launcher, CLI and MCP entry point.
- `@lv24/vigil-<os>-<cpu>` are optionalDependencies containing the platform
  binary. Never install them directly.
- npm installs seven packages: one launcher plus six platform packages
  (win32, darwin and linux; x64 and arm64).
- Do not use --no-optional or --omit=optional; the launcher then has no binary.
- PyPI `lv24-vigil` is a thin launcher that delegates to npm and needs Node.js
  18+. npm is canonical.

## Commands

    vigil scan [path] --no-llm              deterministic rules only, no network
    vigil scan [path]                       add LLM triage if a model is configured
    vigil scan --format json                JSON report on stdout
    vigil scan --format sarif --fail-on high
    vigil review --base origin/main --format sarif
    vigil fix <finding-id>                  print a unified diff
    vigil fix <finding-id> --apply          write the diff, never commit
    vigil threat-model [path]               STRIDE markdown, needs a model
    vigil status --json                     provider, model, rules, store, last scan
    vigil rules [--json]                    authoritative rule catalog
    vigil baseline list|add|remove|clear
    vigil report --format md|json|sarif|html
    vigil precheck --sarif FILE --api URL --token JWT
    vigil hook install [--mode pre-commit|pre-push] [--force] [--fail-on LEVEL]
    vigil hook status
    vigil hook uninstall
    vigil mcp [--root DIR]

Exit codes: 0 clean, 1 error, 2 findings at or above --fail-on.
Default scan path is the current directory.

## Before commit / before deploy

Run the deterministic gate before every commit or handoff:

    vigil scan . --no-llm --fail-on high

Install the local guard once per clone:

    vigil hook install                  # pre-commit
    vigil hook install --mode pre-push  # or before push
    vigil hook status
    vigil hook uninstall

Hooks are marked `# managed by lv24-vigil`, honour `VIGIL_BIN` (default
`vigil`), and refuse to replace a foreign hook without `--force` (backup:
`<hook>.pre-vigil.bak`). CI templates: `examples/github-workflow.yml` (PR, main,
manual dispatch), `examples/gitlab-ci.yml` (MR, default branch, manual web), and
the composite `action.yml`.

Agent rules:

- Run `vigil scan . --no-llm --fail-on high` before committing or deploying.
- Use `vigil hook install` for a local pre-commit or pre-push gate.
- Never auto-apply a fix (`vigil fix --apply` / `vigil_fix apply=true`), never
  commit, stage or push on the user's behalf, and never suppress a finding
  without an explicit baseline decision.
- A `--fail-on` exit code 2 is a policy failure; report it, do not retry it
  away.

## MCP

Server command: `vigil mcp` (stdio, newline-delimited JSON-RPC).
Protocol versions: 2025-06-18, 2025-03-26, 2024-11-05.

OpenCode (`opencode.json`):

    {
      "mcp": {
        "vigil": {
          "type": "local",
          "command": ["npx", "-y", "lv24-vigil", "mcp"],
          "enabled": true
        }
      }
    }

Claude Code:

    claude mcp add vigil -- npx -y lv24-vigil mcp

Codex (`~/.codex/config.toml`):

    [mcp_servers.vigil]
    command = "npx"
    args = ["-y", "lv24-vigil", "mcp"]

Cursor (`~/.cursor/mcp.json`):

    {
      "mcpServers": {
        "vigil": {
          "command": "npx",
          "args": ["-y", "lv24-vigil", "mcp"]
        }
      }
    }

If Vigil is installed globally, use `["vigil", "mcp"]` instead of npx.

## MCP tools

Read-only unless noted.

- vigil_scan(path?, mode?, useLlm?, ...) — scan a repository; writes scan history.
- vigil_review(baseRef?, diff?, ...) — review changed lines; writes scan history.
- vigil_explain(findingId) — explain one finding.
- vigil_fix(findingId, apply?) — propose a diff; apply=true writes source files.
- vigil_threat_model(path?) — STRIDE-style threat model.
- vigil_status() — provider, model, engine and store status.
- vigil_rules(category?, language?, severity?, query?) — rule catalog.
- vigil_baseline(action, ...) — inspect or update the baseline file.
- vigil_report(scanId?, format?, path?) — render a stored scan; writes only with path.
- vigil_verify(findingId) — re-check whether a finding is still present.
- vigil_history(limit?) — recent scans from the local store.

Resources: vigil://status, vigil://rules, vigil://scan/last, vigil://scan/<id>.
Prompts: security_review, threat_model, fix_finding.

## Providers

Set VIGIL_PROVIDER and the provider key, or let Vigil infer the provider from a
known key. Explicit VIGIL_* variables win.

    openai        OPENAI_API_KEY        gpt-4.1-mini
    anthropic     ANTHROPIC_API_KEY     claude-sonnet-4-5
    gemini        GEMINI_API_KEY        gemini-2.5-flash
    openrouter    OPENROUTER_API_KEY    anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5
    groq          GROQ_API_KEY          llama-3.3-70b-versatile
    deepseek      DEEPSEEK_API_KEY      deepseek-chat
    mistral       MISTRAL_API_KEY       mistral-large-latest
    xai           XAI_API_KEY           grok-4-fast
    opencode-go   OPENCODE_API_KEY      deepseek-v4.1-flash
    ollama        none                  qwen2.5-coder:14b
    lmstudio      none                  local-model
    command       none                  local CLI, no API key
    custom        VIGIL_API_KEY         set VIGIL_MODEL and VIGIL_BASE_URL

The `command` provider executes an already-authenticated local CLI (for example
`opencode run`) and must be set in the user config, not in a project file.
OLLAMA_HOST points at a non-default Ollama.

## Rules

163 deterministic rules in eight families:
VGL-SEC 24 secrets, VGL-INJ 37 injection, VGL-CRY 12 crypto, VGL-AUTH 16 auth,
VGL-WEB 17 web, VGL-CFG 28 config/IaC, VGL-CI 17 CI, VGL-DEP 12 dependencies.

VGL-AI-001 is synthesized by the LLM deep review. VGL-OSV-<advisory> appears only
when scan.osv is enabled. `vigil rules` is authoritative.

## Safety

- Scans are read-only; they write only .vigil/scans or the user cache.
- vigil hook install writes .git/hooks/<mode> and may save a .pre-vigil.bak
  backup with --force; uninstall removes only marked hooks.
- vigil fix --apply writes a validated diff; it never commits or stages.
- Baseline, an explicit report path and vigil init write their own files.
- Secrets detected by rules are masked in evidence, snippets and reports.
- Deterministic scans make no network calls.
- LLM features send minimal context only to the configured endpoint.
- Fix paths are confined to the repository; binary, symlink and .git patches are
  rejected; git apply --check runs before any write.
- No telemetry, analytics, account or update check.
- vigil precheck is an explicit upload and requires a staff JWT with
  ops:security-scans; it does not start a scan.
